docs.title: Welcome to DIYABC support tutorial!
docs.text:
This is a beginner-friendly guide to the power of DIYABC (Cornouet et al., 2014), a software designed to carry out ABC-supported coalescent simulations with variant and micro-satellite data from populations and individuals.

You can find DIYABC documentation here and you can also read the supporting paper here.

That being said, let's dive deep into DIYABC!

IMPORTANT TIP: You should first go to the installation page, then follow the tutorials, then go the model selection section and, finally, read the goodness of fit and the parameter estimation portions

docs.title: About DIYABC support tutorial
docs.text:
This is a collection of best practices and suggestion that you should take into account when dealing with DIYABC.

This support tutorial does not cover all possible use cases and options, but is a good way to get started and reach an intermediate level of analysis with DIYABC.

This is supposed to be free learning material, and it is distributed under an MIT license.

This tutorial might contain errors or things that can be improved, so you can refer to the contribution page if you want to report/correct/enhance anything.

docs.title: Contributing to DIYABC support tutorial
docs.text: Do you want to contribute to this project? Make sure to read this guidelines first :)

docs.title: Issue
docs.text:
When to do it:

  • You found errors but you don't know how to solve them or don't have time/will to do the solve
  • You want new features but you don't know how to implement them or don't have time/will to do the implementation

⚠️ Always check open and closed issues before you submit yours to avoid duplicates

How to do it:

  • Open an issue
  • Give the issue a meaningful title (short but effective problem description)
  • Describe the problem following the issue template

docs.title: Traditional contribution
docs.text:
When to do it:

  • You found bugs and corrected them
  • You optimized/improved the code
  • You added new features that you think could be useful to others

How to do it:

  1. Fork this repository
  2. Commit your changes
  3. Submit pull request (make sure to provide a thorough description of the changes)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Installing DIYABC should be easy: you just need to grab the pre-built release the best suits your platform (Windows, MacOS or Linux) from the releases page.

The file should be executable and, once you download it, you can rename it as diyabc and run, to test the successful installation:

# on macOS/Linux
diyabc -h
# on Windows
.\diyabc.exe -h

If you're not lucky, and for some reasons this first approach does not work, then you should proceed with this second approach, i.e. building the code from source, although it requires a little bit more programming and is suitable only for Linux/macOS.

  • First of all, you need to check that cmake is installed:
cmake --version
  • If cmake is not installed, then proceed to install it:
# from package resources
sudo apt-get -y install cmake # Ubuntu
# with conda
conda install -y conda-forge::cmake
# with brew
brew install cmake
  • Once cmake is installed, clone DIYABC repository:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/diyabc/diyabc.git
cd diyabc
  • Create a build folder
mkdir build
cd build
  • Pre-build DIYABC
cmake ../
  • Build DIYABC
cmake --build . --config Release

You will find diyabc executable under diyabc/build/src-JMC-C++/general

Now we can just copy the binary file in our working directory:

cd ../..
cp diyabc/build/src-JMC-C++/general diyabc

And we can optionally remove the diyabc repository we compiled as it is no longer necessary:

rm -rf diyabc/

And then we can test the installation by running:

./diyabc -h

With this, you should be able to successfully install DIYABC. Now, let's follow with some examples!

Before you start
docs.text:
There are some important things that you should take into account before reading this tutorial section:

  • Keep in mind that there are many use cases for DIYABC: we will focus only on POPULATION DATA based on SNPs
  • We will be using some R programming language, so it will be useful for you to have a little bit of knowledge about it. If you do not know anything about R, here is a free and complete 2 hours introduction to it
  • You can find all the code resources here and all the data here
  • You should follow these steps:
    • First of all, understand how we generate data
    • Second, read about how we approach DIYABC
    • Third, follow up with Tutorial 1 and Tutorial 2

docs.title: How to approach DIYABC?
docs.text:
Disclaimer: This are best practice that worked for me, that does not necessarily mean that will work universally

DIYABC offers you the possibility of running a certain number of simulations with a specified number of data units (we will work with SNPs from now on).

The workflow that I follow is pretty much this:

  • Multi-turn simulations aimed at model selection: In this phase, you run simulations on sets of similar scenarios, extracting the best and re-using it in other simulations with different sets of scenarios. At the end of this phase, you will have the absolute winner for all your scenarios. We will discuss what and why to perform model selection in detail later. For this phase, it is advise to run quick simulations with 2000 SNPs and 2000 iterations per scenario (which means that if you have 10 scenarios you should run a total of 20000 iterations).
  • Goodness of fit and parameters estimation: In this phase, you take the best scenario overall and simulate for (at least) 50000 iterations with 2000 or more SNPs. This will allow you to run Goodness of Fit tests and parameter estimation.
